newsitem.title: USA: US cash crudes sustain grade gains, outrights drop.
newsitem.headline: US cash crudes sustain grade gains, outrights drop.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes ended Thursday stronger for domestic grade differentials at the same time outright crude prices floundered badly.
NYMEX March futures went off the board after Thursday's session, limping off the screen with losses putting the March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing 80 cents lower at $21.95-$22.05 a barrel.
Late in the session, cash traders said the March/April WTI roll was traded at 30 cts, putting the March outright at slightly weaker levels than the late afternoon.
The Mar/Apr roll started the session at more than 45 cts.
Cash traders said refiner buying interest pushed the Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James diffs to sales to 39 cts over the WTI/Cushing, 11 cts higher than deals seen late Wednesday.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire charted a steady to slightly firmer course, talked late at 5-15 cts over the WTI/Cushing.
Midland/WTI was last done at 39 cts under the WTI/Cushing, at the weaker end of a narrow trading range.
West Texas Sour/Midland was done last at a $2.35 discount to the WTI/Cushing, slightly weaker than Wednesday, but 12-14 cts lower than trades earlier in the same session.

Sours were seen under growing pressure due to an abundance of supply from West Coast markets, Canada and Iraq. Last week, Basrah Light cargo-holder Bayoil Trading was heard offering an early March delivery into the U.S. Gulf at Mar WTI -$1.70.
Bayoil met with such a disinterested market that the cargo was to be offered at April WTI -$2.00 for April delivery.

Other trades had Eugene Island sold at a $2.20 discount to the WTI/Cushing. March Postings were done late at $2.04, after selling earlier some 20-25 cts higher, ahead of the collapse in the Mar/Apr roll, traders said.
